title: Field Report: Control System Anomaly — Chemical Building

fields.organization: City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer — Operations Division
fields.location: Chemical Building, Level 1, Control Room and North Service Corridor
fields.summary: Review of PACS access logs for the Chemical Building from 09:55 to 10:05 confirms no unauthorized access events, door override codes, or alarm triggers. The HMI shows the east door closed and locked at 09:58:33. PSH-302 has not tripped. Physical safety systems are not engaged. However, lab results confirm finished-water pH is 9.3 and caustic dose is 38 mg/L — both far above safe limits. The HMI displays NAOH-FC-203 at 14 mg/L, within normal band. This indicates a control-system mismatch. No physical breach occurred. The system is compromised.

findings.notes: HMI and PACS show closed and locked at 09:58:33; no alarms or overrides recorded
No trip recorded; still in normal state
Displays 14 mg/L — within normal band
Reads 9.3 — exceeds safe upper limit of 9.5
Lab confirms 38 mg/L — exceeds PLC hard limit of 40 mg/L
Manual override to 0 mg/L failed — pump remains running
Still shows 'AUTO' and 'Running' — no change after manual override
Running at full speed; tank level dropping
No visible leaks or pressure drops
No unauthorized entries or failed access attempts in timeframe

actionsTaken: Reviewed PACS badge and CAM-01 to CAM-10 camera logs for 09:55–10:05 via MBW-NVR-01
Verified HMI and PACS status for east door at 09:58:33
Notified Incident Commander and SCADA / IT Security Manager via DWS-1
recommendations: Activate Section 7.1 manual operation protocol under ERP Section 7.5
Isolate MBW-HMI-02 and PLC-02 from remote access until forensic review complete
Initiate chain-of-custody for SEC-4 evidence form (SEC-4-2026-1022-082212)
fields.photosNote: 4 photos attached: IMG_2026-0015-01 (HMI NAOH-FC-203 display), IMG_2026-0015-02 (field pH readout), IMG_2026-0015-03 (caustic pump running), IMG_2026-0015-04 (PLC-02 panel) — all timestamped 10:32

instructorNote: This inject confirms the HMI is lying. The IC must now order full manual operations and validate the lab results as the sole reliable source. Watch for hesitation in accepting lab data over HMI.
